data.one_liner: Compression framework providing FFI implementations for Brotli, Lz4, and Zstd.
data.what_it_does: Provides a compression framework in Dart with FFI implementations for Brotli, Lz4, and Zstd (Zstandard), along with ready-to-use prebuilt binaries for Windows, Linux, and macOS. It also includes an executable tool 'escompress' for command-line file compression.
use_when: You need Brotli, Lz4, or Zstd compression algorithms in your Dart or Flutter application.
You want FFI-based performance for compression tasks on desktop or mobile platforms.
You need a command-line tool to encode/decode compressed files.
avoid_when: You are running heavily on the web where native FFI shared libraries are unavailable and require pure Dart solutions.
You only require basic GZip compression which is already built into the standard Dart SDK (`dart:io`).
strengths: Supports multiple efficient compression algorithms (Brotli, Lz4, Zstd).
Comes with ready-to-use prebuilt binaries for major desktop and mobile environments.
Flexible library loader supporting custom paths and environment variables.
weaknesses: Requires managing and bundling native shared libraries (.dll, .so, .dylib) for target platforms.
Mac OS binaries require manual security allowance unless signed.
data.setup_notes: FFI-based implementations require access to native shared libraries (.dll, .so, .dylib). Android projects require placing prebuilt .so files in jniLibs and updating build.gradle.
